entries.title: Use of GLP-1 medicines shifts towards obesity treatment in Europe, new study shows
entries.description: A large European real-world evidence study has shown that the use of GLP-1 medicines has changed substantially over the past decade. Originally authorised for type 2 diabetes,…
entries.summary: Use of GLP‑1 medicines in Europe has shifted from primarily treating type 2 diabetes to increasingly addressing obesity over the past decade.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should monitor labeling and reimbursement changes for these biologics as they are now being prescribed for obesity, affecting regulatory submissions and post‑marketing commitments.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Qualifying notice amendment for Jaypirca (304233)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada issued a Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) for Jaypirca, allowing marketing pending additional benefit studies.
entries.why_it_matters: The RA team must monitor the compliance conditions and ensure the sponsor completes the required studies to maintain approval.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved the first medicine for treating limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9), a rare inherited muscle disease, for adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.
entries.summary: FDA approves first treatment for limb‑girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 for patients weighing at least 30 kg.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must update labeling and ensure inclusion of adult and pediatric patients ≥30 kg for this newly approved biologic.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First New Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer in More Than 20 Years
entries.description: The FDA today approved Wilserdly (giredestrant), used alone after surgery in adults with estrogen receptor–positive, HER2-negative breast cancer — the most common subtype of the disease.
entries.summary: The FDA approved Wilserdly (giredestrant) for use alone after surgery in adults with early‑stage estrogen receptor–positive, HER2‑negative breast cancer.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should update product labeling and consider this new therapy for eligible patients, impacting labeling, IND submissions, and reimbursement strategies.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease
entries.description: FDA today approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg (approximately 33 pounds).
entries.summary: The FDA has approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets for treating neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware that this new small‑molecule therapy is now available for adult and pediatric GD3 patients weighing at least 15 kg, impacting labeling and reimbursement processes.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide
entries.description: FDA  today announced the Global Reliance Disclosure Program (GRDP), a landmark initiative that will fundamentally transform how the FDA's regulatory drug and biologic approval decisions are leveraged by health authorities around the world.
entries.summary: The FDA has launched the Global Reliance Disclosure Program (GRDP) to allow other health authorities to use FDA regulatory decisions to support their own drug and biologic approvals.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must be aware of GRDP so they can anticipate that FDA decisions may influence global market approvals and potentially streamline regulatory pathways for their products.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer
entries.description: FDA approved Lembaz (adrabetadex) injection, the first treatment shown to help people with a severe form of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) live longer.
entries.summary: FDA approves Lembaz (adrabetadex) injection, the first drug shown to extend life in patients with infantile-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should note that this biologic therapy is now available for a rare, severe neurodegenerative disease, impacting patient access and reimbursement strategies.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
entries.description: FDA today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or a high-risk transient ischemic attack.
entries.summary: FDA approves the first factor XIa inhibitor, Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, for stroke prevention in certain adults.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must add this new therapy to their product portfolio and update labeling for patients at high risk of stroke after mild‑to‑moderate non‑cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high‑risk TIA.

entries.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherap
entries.summary: FDA granted accelerated approval for Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase‑lpuj) for adults with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC progressing after platinum‑based therapy.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling biologics for oncology must update labeling, prescribing information, and monitoring plans to reflect the new accelerated approval and its indications.

entries.description: This new guideline provides comprehensive clinical protocol organization with standardized content, with a Template which presents the format and structure of the protocol, including the table of contents, common headers, and contents; and a Technical Specification which presents the conformance, cardinality, and other technical attributes that enable the interoperable electronic exchange of protocol content.
entries.summary: Phased implementation of the ICH M11 guideline for Clinical electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP) has been announced.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must update protocol templates and technical specifications to comply with the new standardized structure and electronic exchange requirements.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice to stakeholders on implementing ICH M13B: Bioequivalence for immediate release solid oral dosage forms: Additional strengths biowaiver
entries.description: Part of the foreseen ICH M13 Guideline series (M13A-C), the ICH M13B Guideline is intended to provide recommendations on obtaining waivers of bioequivalence (BE) studies for one or more additional strengths of a drug product in an application where in vivo BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths. This guideline is applicable to both development and post approval phases for orally administered immediate-release (IR) solid oral dosage forms designed to deliver drugs to the systemic circulation, such as tablets, capsules, and granules/powders for oral suspension. The ICH M13B Guideline is the second Guideline in the foreseen series to describe the scientific and technical aspects of demonstrating BE for additional strengths of a drug product, i.e., obtaining waiver(s) for one or more strengths in an application with multiple strengths when BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths following ICH M13A. How regulatory decisions may be made based on BE assessment is out of the scope of this guideline.
entries.summary: The new ICH M13B guideline allows biowaivers for additional strengths of immediate‑release solid oral dosage forms when one strength has already demonstrated bioequivalence.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams developing or approving multi‑strength IR tablets, capsules or powders must now assess whether additional strengths can be waived, potentially saving time and resources.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: ICH guidelines implemented by Health Canada
entries.description: Health Canada has implemented and launched public consultations on several International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, reflecting Canada’s ongoing commitment to global regulatory harmonization. Stakeholders are encouraged to review and provide feedback on the draft guidelines for consultation by the respective deadlines, as Health Canada will forward all comments to the ICH for consideration in the finalization process. Health Canada has begun implementing finalized guidelines. Stakeholders are encouraged to integrate these guidelines into their drug registration processes.
entries.summary: Health Canada has launched public consultations on several ICH guidelines.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review and provide feedback on the draft guidelines to influence their finalization and integration into drug registration processes.

Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada grants a Notice of Compliance with Conditions for Calquence, requiring additional studies to confirm clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: The RA team must plan and oversee the required post‑approval studies to meet conditions and maintain market authorization.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards.
entries.summary: FDA issued final guidance clarifying how cellular and gene therapy manufacturers should implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan to ensure potency standards are met.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams working on cell and gene therapy products must incorporate these potency planning requirements into their development and quality programs.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Plasmid DNA-based Immunotherapy for Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) for treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP).
entries.summary: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Voceryq, a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy, for treating adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must update product labeling, regulatory submissions, and monitoring plans to reflect the new approval and ensure compliance with accelerated approval requirements.
